newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia farmers urge no business budget cut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia farmers urge no business budget cut.

text.p: Australia's National Farmers Federation on Wednesday urged the government not to target the business sector in 1997/98 budget savings.

"Our (pre-budget) submission suggests that a further round of fiscal tightening will be needed to meet the government's commitment, and the federation would support such a move without cuts unfairly impinging on the business sectors," federation economic committee chairman John Watson said in a statement.

"It is imperative that the government does not impose new or increased taxes on productive inputs, or spending reductions which limit the innovativeness and productive capacity of business," Watson said.
In its submission to the government the federation said the cuts to the business sector in the government's 1996/97 budget had unfairly constrained the productive sectors.
The government announced budget measures in August that would save about A$7 billion in the fiscal year to June 1998.
Since then the government's finances have deteriorated further and Treasurer Peter Costello said further savings -- less than A$4 billion -- would be announced in his May budget.
The federation said the 1997/98 budget should continue to pursue an underlying balance on average through the ups and downs of the economic cycle and it should focus on wide-ranging tax reform.
